name: Lenalidomide (single-agent, high-risk smoldering myeloma)

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Single-agent lenalidomide is offered for high-risk smoldering myeloma to delay progression to active disease; a clinical trial remains the preferred pathway. It is not biomarker-restricted. Physician decides.

treatmentSetting: early intervention for high-risk smoldering (asymptomatic) myeloma
supportiveCare: Lenalidomide: VTE thromboprophylaxis (aspirin for standard risk) and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen); dose-adjust for renal impairment.
Counsel on second-primary-malignancy risk with prolonged lenalidomide exposure.
Treat as active myeloma once a myeloma-defining event appears.
monitoring: CBC with differential and platelets before each cycle
M-protein and serum free light chains for progression

doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume lenalidomide at a reduced dose per labeling for grade 3 to 4 cytopenia; clinical review.

drugs.name: Lenalidomide
drugs.notes: Lenalidomide 25 mg PO once daily on days 1 to 21 of each 28-day cycle, continued until progression or intolerance. Dose is reduced for renal impairment or cytopenias. This mirrors the single-agent early-intervention schedule studied in high-risk smoldering myeloma; a lower continuous dose is sometimes used for tolerance. Requires VTE thromboprophylaxis and REMS-program dispensing (teratogen). Own wording from standard-of-care knowledge; physician decides.
